preconditions.description: Input integers n and k must satisfy 2 ≤ k < n ≤ 1000.
Input consists of exactly two integers n and k separated by whitespace.

postconditions.description: Output consists of two lines: the first line is the minimum number of colors c, and the second line is a valid edge coloring with exactly c distinct colors.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= color <= c for color in color_list) and len(set(color_list)) == c
postconditions.description: All colors in the output coloring are integers between 1 and c, and exactly c distinct colors are used.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a < b <= n for a, b in [(i//n + 1, i%n + 1) for i in range(n*(n-1)//2)])
postconditions.description: The edge coloring corresponds to edges in increasing order of start node, then end node, covering all possible directed edges a < b.

postconditions.expression: c == 2 if k == n-1 else (c == 2 if k >= (n-1)//2 + 1 else c == 3)
postconditions.description: The minimum number of colors c is 2 if k is large enough (k ≥ (n-1)//2 + 1) or k = n-1, otherwise it is 3.

postconditions.expression: all(any(color_list[i] != color_list[j] for j in range(i+1, i+k)) for i in range(len(color_list)-k+1))
postconditions.description: For every path of length k (i.e., every sequence of k consecutive edges in the coloring), there are at least 2 distinct colors.

repair_issue.instruction: The expression does not correctly capture the requirement for rainbow paths of length k. The current expression checks for any two distinct colors in a sliding window of size k, but it does not account for the fact that the path must be a valid sequence of edges in the directed graph (a < b < c < ...). The expression must ensure that for every valid path of length k (i.e., a sequence of edges (a1,a2), (a2,a3), ..., (ak,ak+1) where a1 < a2 < ... < ak+1), there are at least 2 distinct colors.
repair_issue.task_evidence: A rainbow path of length x is defined as a path in the graph such that there exists at least 2 distinct colors among the set of x edges.
